content: Etravirine can decrease the levels or effects of certain drugs by influencing their metabolism through hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, CYP2C9/10, and CYP2C19. In some cases, co-administration of etravirine with specific drugs is contraindicated, while in others, alternative therapies or close monitoring are recommended. Below are key interactions: 1. Etravirine and Palovarotene: Etravirine reduces palovarotene levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Etravirine and Panobinostat: Etravirine decreases panobinostat levels significantly (~70%), potentially leading to treatment failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 3. Etravirine and Pantoprazole: Etravirine reduces pantoprazole levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. 4. Etravirine and Parecoxib: Etravirine interacts with parecoxib, altering its levels through CYP2C19, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 metabolism. The effects are minor but require close monitoring. 5. Etravirine and Pazopanib: Etravirine decreases pazopanib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Etravirine and Peginterferon Alfa-2b: Peginterferon alfa-2b reduces etravirine levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Etravirine and Pemigatinib: Etravirine decreases pemigatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 8. Etravirine and Pentamidine: Etravirine increases pentamidine levels through CYP2C19 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Etravirine and Pentobarbital: Pentobarbital decreases etravirine levels by affecting CYP2C19, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Etravirine and Phenytoin: Phenytoin significantly reduces etravirine levels by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Etravirine and Pimavanserin: Etravirine reduces pimavanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration if possible, and monitor for reduced efficacy. 12. Etravirine and Pimozide: Etravirine decreases pimozide levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 13. Etravirine and Pioglitazone: Etravirine reduces pioglitazone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 14. Etravirine and Piroxicam: Etravirine increases piroxicam levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 15. Etravirine and Pirtobrutinib: Etravirine decreases pirtobrutinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, adjust the pirtobrutinib dose and monitor closely. 16. Etravirine and Pitolisant: Etravirine reduces pitolisant levels by 50% via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 17. Etravirine and Polatuzumab Vedotin: Etravirine decreases polatuzumab vedotin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Etravirine and Pomalidomide: Etravirine affects pomalidomide levels through CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Etravirine and Ponatinib: Etravirine reduces ponatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 20. Etravirine and Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Etravirine and Pralsetinib: Etravirine decreases pralsetinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, double the pralsetinib dose starting on day 7 and resume the previous dose 14 days after discontinuing etravirine. 22. Etravirine and Praziquantel: Etravirine reduces praziquantel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Discontinue etravirine two weeks before starting praziquantel. 23. Etravirine and Prednisone: Etravirine reduces prednisone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Etravirine and Pretomanid: Etravirine decreases pretomanid levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Etravirine and Primidone: Primidone reduces etravirine levels via CYP2C19, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Etravirine and Progesterone (various forms): Etravirine reduces progesterone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Etravirine and Propafenone: Etravirine decreases propafenone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 28. Etravirine and Quetiapine: Etravirine reduces quetiapine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Etravirine and Quinidine: Etravirine decreases quinidine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Etravirine and Quinine: Etravirine reduces quinine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 31. Etravirine and Quinupristin/Dalfopristin: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Etravirine and Quizartinib: Etravirine decreases quizartinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Etravirine and Rabeprazole: Etravirine reduces rabeprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 34. Etravirine and Ramelteon: Etravirine affects ramelteon levels through CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 35. Etravirine and Ranolazine: Etravirine reduces ranolazine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 36. Etravirine and Regorafenib: Etravirine decreases regorafenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 37. Etravirine and Repaglinide: Etravirine reduces repaglinide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Etravirine and Rilpivirine: Etravirine reduces rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 39. Etravirine and Rimegepant: Etravirine affects rimegepant levels through CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Etravirine and Riociguat: Etravirine reduces riociguat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 41. Etravirine and Ripretinib: Etravirine decreases ripretinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Etravirine and Rivaroxaban: Etravirine reduces rivaroxaban levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Etravirine and Roflumilast: Etravirine decreases roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 44. Etravirine and Rolapitant: Etravirine reduces rolapitant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Etravirine and Romidepsin: Etravirine decreases romidepsin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 46. Etravirine and Rufinamide: Rufinamide reduces etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Etravirine and Ruxolitinib (topical): Etravirine reduces ruxolitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 48. Etravirine and Saxagliptin: Etravirine reduces saxagliptin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 49. Etravirine and Selpercatinib: Etravirine decreases selpercatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 50. Etravirine and Selumetinib: Etravirine reduces selumetinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 51. Etravirine and Sildenafil: Etravirine reduces sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Etravirine and Silodosin: Etravirine reduces silodosin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 53. Etravirine and Simvastatin: Etravirine reduces simvastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 54. Etravirine and Siponimod: Etravirine affects siponimod levels through CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 55. Etravirine and Sirolimus: Etravirine reduces sirolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 56. Etravirine and Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Etravirine reduces velpatasvir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 57. Etravirine and Solifenacin: Etravirine reduces solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Etravirine and Sonidegib: Etravirine reduces sonidegib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 59. Etravirine and Sorafenib: Etravirine reduces sorafenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Etravirine and Sparsentan: Sparsentan reduces etravirine levels via CYP2C9/10 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Etravirine and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort reduces etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 62. Etravirine and Stiripentol: Stiripentol affects etravirine levels through CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 63. Etravirine and Sufentanil: Etravirine reduces sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 64. Etravirine and Sulfamethoxazole: Etravirine affects sulfamethoxazole levels through CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. 65. Etravirine and Sunitinib: Etravirine reduces sunitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Etravirine and Suvorexant: Etravirine reduces suvorexant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Etravirine and Tacrolimus: Etravirine reduces tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Etravirine and Tadalafil: Etravirine reduces tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Etravirine and Tamoxifen: Etravirine affects tamoxifen levels through CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Etravirine and Tamsulosin: Etravirine reduces tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Etravirine and Tasimelteon: Etravirine reduces tasimelteon levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 72. Etravirine and Tazemetostat: Etravirine reduces tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 73. Etravirine and Tecovirimat: Tecovirimat affects etravirine levels through CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 74. Etravirine and Temsirolimus: Etravirine reduces temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 75. Etravirine and Teniposide: Etravirine reduces teniposide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 76. Etravirine and Terbinafine: Etravirine reduces terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 77. Etravirine and Tetracycline: Etravirine reduces tetracycline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 78. Etravirine and Tezacaftor: Etravirine reduces tezacaftor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 79. Etravirine and Theophylline: Etravirine reduces theophylline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 80. Etravirine and Tiagabine: Etravirine reduces tiagabine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 81. Etravirine and Ticagrelor: Etravirine reduces ticagrelor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with potent CYP3A inducers. 82. Etravirine and Ticlopidine: Ticlopidine increases etravirine levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism, while etravirine reduces ticlopidine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. This summary provides a detailed overview of the interactions between etravirine and other drugs, emphasizing the need for caution, monitoring, or alternative therapies in specific cases.
